findings.topic: profileData.ts reference comment (verbatim, per task)
findings.fact: src/lib/profile/profileData.ts:170-171 verbatim: "// Profiles are children of the member's person (`_parent` = personId), mirroring listMyRsvps' native own-person scoping. Project `_sharing` (underscore) — a bare `sharing` projection silently returns empty (entu-api utils/entity.js:198). A member has up to three profile entities; limit=10 is an explicit, ample bound." findings.topic: seasonManage.ts under-reporting admission (verbatim, per task) + its exact site
findings.fact: src/lib/seasons/seasonManage.ts:456-464, the doc comment directly above `countSeriesOccurrences` (fn at line 465): "How many occurrence events the series holds RIGHT NOW — the number the panel's two-step confirm shows before arming an irreversible cascade (#197 review 2nd pass F2). Deliberately its own one-row read of the server's `count`, not the panel list's client-side tally: the list derives its counts from ONE season-wide `limit=500` event read, so it under-reports a big season and misses anything created since it last ran, and the confirm must not promise a number the write never checks." Echoed (not re-sourced) in a comment at src/routes/+page.svelte:2941-2947. Functionally answered already by `countSeriesOccurrences` (own limit=1 count-only read, lines 465-480) and by `countSeasonScope`/`readSeasonScope` (lines 605-669) which use `listChildIds`/`listSeasonEvents` with `CHILD_READ_LIMIT=500` and an explicit throw when `count > entities.length` — i.e. refuse rather than promise a wrong number.
findings.evidence: Read src/lib/seasons/seasonManage.ts in full (1-680); grepped +page.svelte:2945, confirmed it's a pointer comment, not a second query site.

findings.topic: Cascade reads already refuse-not-truncate — a third pattern the issue's (1)/(2) binary doesn't name
findings.fact: `listChildIds` (seasonManage.ts:418-442, `CHILD_READ_LIMIT=500`, used for event_series/repertoire_item/event/attendance/program_item cascade-delete work-lists) and `listSeasonEvents` (line 646-669) both read `count` off the wire body and THROW ('nothing was deleted') when `count > entities.length`. These `limit=500` reads never silently act on a partial list. Sites: seasonManage.ts:427 (generic childType) and seasonManage.ts:654 (season's event children with `_parent`). Neither is class (1) 'provably unreachable' (500 children under one season/event IS reachable) nor class (2) 'tell the user it's partial' (there's no display — these feed a destructive-cascade decision) — they're a third, already-safe shape worth keeping distinct from both classes.
findings.evidence: Read seasonManage.ts:400-442 and 624-669, the explicit `if (total > ids.length) throw` in both functions.

findings.topic: Is a read-result count available at render time (client-side truncation signal)
findings.fact: No. Every render-path list function types its parsed response as only `{ entities?: [...] }` (listWorks, listEditions, listCopies, listLendings in libraryData.ts; listActiveMembers/listArchivedMembers in rosterData.ts; listSections in sectionData.ts; listLinks in linkData.ts; listSeasons/listEventsForSeason in entuSeasons.ts; listRepertoireItems/listProgramItems in repertoireData.ts) — the server's `count` field, when present, is discarded by the type cast and never read. The only signal derivable without changing any response type is `entities.length === limit` — an unreliable heuristic (a collection with exactly `limit` rows and nothing beyond gives a false positive) — and no surface currently even computes that.
findings.evidence: Read src/lib/library/libraryData.ts:24-36 (listWorks body type is `{ entities?: [...] }`, no `count`); grep -n 'count' across libraryData.ts, rosterData.ts, sectionData.ts, linkData.ts, entuSeasons.ts, repertoireData.ts, attendanceData.ts, rsvpData.ts returned no `body.count` reads outside seasonManage.ts.

findings.topic: Server-count precedent #1 — countSeriesOccurrences (issue's cited example)
findings.fact: seasonManage.ts:452-476, verbatim comment: 'Deliberately its own one-row read of the server's count, not the panel list's client-side tally: the list derives its counts from ONE season-wide limit=500 event read, so it under-reports a big season and misses anything created since it last ran.' Wire shape: GET `entity?_type.string=event&_parent.reference={seriesId}&props=_id&limit=1`, response body typed `{ count?: number; entities?: unknown[] }`, function returns `body.count ?? body.entities?.length ?? 0`. This is a SEPARATE dedicated request from the list read it audits — used only to compute the number shown in the two-step delete confirm, not the render.
findings.evidence: Read src/lib/seasons/seasonManage.ts lines 440-476 this session.

findings.topic: Server-count precedent #2 — listChildIds cascade guard (more directly reusable than #1)
findings.fact: seasonManage.ts:399-440 (`listChildIds`, used by the event/season cascade-delete refusal) reads `count` from the SAME capped list request it already makes for the delete's own work list — `entity?_type.string=${childType}&_parent.reference=${parentId}&props=_id&limit=${CHILD_READ_LIMIT}` (CHILD_READ_LIMIT=500) — parses `{ count?: number; entities?: [...] }`, computes `total = body.count ?? ids.length`, and throws when `total > ids.length` ('has {total} {childType} children, more than the {LIMIT}-row cascade read can carry — nothing was deleted'). Unlike countSeriesOccurrences, this needs no second HTTP request: it is the render-facing pattern's closest reusable ancestor — widen the existing list-read's response type to keep `count` and compare it to the returned array length.
findings.evidence: Read src/lib/seasons/seasonManage.ts lines 395-440 this session; the same shape recurs at line ~654-665 for the season-level event-child cascade check.

findings.topic: i18n mechanics for a new partial-list string
findings.fact: Messages live in four flat JSON files: messages/en.json, et.json, lv.json, uk.json (644/644/645/646 top-level keys respectively — small existing drift, not investigated further). Keys are feature-prefixed (`links_*`, `roster_*`, `library_*`, `agenda_*`, `repertoire_*`, `profile_*`) and each feature's keys are added identically across the locale files (verified for the `links_*` set: title/empty/load_error/retry/no_collective/add_*/edit/save/cancel/remove/move_up/move_down present verbatim in en, et, lv). Consumption is `import { m } from '$lib/paraglide/messages.js'` then `m.<key>()` (or with a param object for interpolated strings, e.g. `m.profile_link_success({ collective })`). A new 'list is partial' string would follow this exact per-feature four-locale key pattern.
findings.evidence: Read messages/en.json, et.json, lv.json around the links_* block; grep for the import line in src/routes/links/+page.svelte:22; grep -c key counts across the four files, run this session.

findings.topic: a11y shape of existing status/notice text on these surfaces
findings.fact: Two established patterns, no third: (1) role="alert" for load/write failures — feature-scoped, visible, red text, `data-testid="<feature>-load-error"` (library-load-error, roster-load-error, roster-sections-load-error, links-load-error, librarian-load-error) plus many inline per-row alert paragraphs for save/checkout/reorder failures. (2) role="status" aria-live="polite" for transient action-confirmation text — almost always `class="sr-only"` and tied to one specific action (create-work-status, create-edition-status-{workId}, library-edition-files-status-{editionId}, roster-reorder-status; bulk-checkout-availability is the one visible non-sr-only status). There is NO existing pattern for a persistent, always-visible informational notice that is neither an error nor a fired-once confirmation — a 'this list is partial' notice that needs to stay up for as long as the condition holds doesn't match either shape as-is.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'aria-live|role="status"|role="alert"' across src/routes/library/+page.svelte, roster/+page.svelte, links/+page.svelte, +page.svelte, agenda components, run this session; read the surrounding markup at several hit lines (library/+page.svelte:1251/1706/1815, roster/+page.svelte:4435/4468-4507).

findings.topic: Does any surface already handle the exactly-at-cap case
findings.fact: No. grep for `.length === <limit-value>`, `.length >= <limit-value>`, and the two limit constants (`CHILD_READ_LIMIT`, the literal 500/200/50/1000/10 caps) across all of src/lib and src/routes found zero cap-detection comparisons on any render path. Every `.length === N` hit in the codebase is an empty-state check (`=== 0` or `=== 1`) unrelated to truncation. The only two places in the whole tree that compare a total against a limit at all are the write-side cascade guards in seasonManage.ts (`listChildIds`'s `total > ids.length` at line ~438, and the mirrored season-level check at ~665) — both refusal gates on irreversible deletes, not render-time notices.
findings.evidence: grep -rn for '.length *===', '.length *>=', literal cap values, and 'CHILD_READ_LIMIT' across src/lib and src/routes (excluding *.spec.ts), run this session; manually reviewed every hit.

findings.topic: 2. Wire layer — how limit is passed
findings.fact: No centralized limit/query-building helper. `entuFetch(db, pathAndQuery, token, init, fetchImpl)` in src/lib/entu/request.ts takes pathAndQuery as an opaque string; every one of the 24 non-spec src/lib files that queries lists builds its own literal query string inline (e.g. `entity?_type.string=work&props=name,composer&limit=500`). `limit=` values are hardcoded per call site, not read from a shared constant, EXCEPT `CHILD_READ_LIMIT = 500` in seasonManage.ts (used for the two #197 cascade-delete guard reads only, not shared with any display-list read).
findings.evidence: Read src/lib/entu/request.ts in full — entuUrl/entuFetch take a raw pathAndQuery string, no limit/query builder; grep -rln 'limit=' src --include='*.ts' | grep -v spec -> 24 files, each with its own inline query string (listed in full)

findings.topic: 2. seasonManage.ts countSeriesOccurrences precedent — exact params
findings.fact: `entity?_type.string=event&_parent.reference={id}&props=_id&limit=1`, response typed `{ count?: number; entities?: unknown[] }`, returns `body.count ?? body.entities?.length ?? 0`. This is the count-only read pattern: minimal props (`_id` only), `limit=1` to keep payload to one row, and the server's own `count` field is what's actually consumed — the one entity in the array is discarded.
findings.evidence: src/lib/seasons/seasonManage.ts lines 465-480, read directly

findings.topic: 2. Entu list responses already carry a total count
findings.fact: The Entu list endpoint (`GET {db}/entity?...`) returns `{ count, entities }` — established from code, not memory. At least 6 call sites already type and read `count`: seasonManage.ts (countSeriesOccurrences, countSeasonScope's CHILD_READ_LIMIT guard x2), sectionActions.ts (`countOf` helper, comment: 'Only the response count is read (limit=1 keeps the payload to one)'), collectiveName.ts (`EntuSearchResponse` type, comment 'Search response envelope for GET {db}/entity?... (count + entities)'), marker.ts (same marker-existence check pattern). Meanwhile roughly 15 other list-reading modules that RENDER lists to the user (repertoireData.ts x2, linkData.ts, libraryData.ts x5 query sites, rosterData.ts x2, scheduleData.ts, entuSeasons.ts x2, attendanceData.ts x3, rsvpData.ts, eventDetail.ts, memberLifecycle.ts, sectionData.ts) type their response as `{ entities?: X[] }` ONLY — no `count` field at all — and so discard whatever count the server sent back, even though nothing in the code suggests count is absent from those responses; they simply never look.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'entities:' src/lib --include='*.ts' | grep -v spec, cross-referenced against the count?:number-typed sites in seasonManage.ts, sectionActions.ts, collectiveName.ts, marker.ts; read collectiveName.ts lines 30-40 (explicit 'count + entities' comment) and repertoireData.ts lines 40-62 (no count in type) directly

findings.topic: 2. Implication for #321's scope
findings.fact: [speculative] If Entu's count field is present on every list response regardless of query shape (documented in-code as a general envelope, not verified live this turn), then detecting 'this list is partial' for most limit=500/200/50 display reads may not need pagination, a second request, or a new API capability at all — just widening the response type to include `count` and comparing it against `entities.length` (or against the limit), the same move sectionActions.ts and seasonManage.ts already made for their guard reads. That would make most of #321's item-2 classifications ('reachable → say so') cheap type+comparison changes rather than UI-architecture work. Whether count is reliably populated for every props/limit combination used by the display-list call sites is [unverified] without a live probe — flagging as a probe candidate.

Overlap with #289 is minimal (disjoint file sets, one incidental shared file rosterData.ts on different lines); #318/#319 confirmed unrelated; #320 confirmed docs-only.
